exact_claim: For the inherited static Q scalar/scale/isothermal-fluid action with C,cs squared,J,S0,a_ref>0 and initial B=0,rho=rho_*>0, finite chi_*,w_*,phi_*, there exists a unique local two-sided positive-density regular-class solution using B as independent coordinate. Its signed g is asymptotic to sgn(x)sqrt(a_* C rho_* abs(x)); phi and rho are C^(1,1/2), W^(2,p) for p<2, and not H2 across the crossing, while B is C^(2,1/2) and chi C^(3,1/2). The distributional equations have no delta source and static energy is locally finite. The bounded full directional Hessian on H1_0 triples has no positive standard product-H1 coercivity constant: localized phi-only test energies tend to zero at fixed derivative norm because A is asymptotic to a positive constant times sqrt(abs(x)). This is not a negative-energy, ghost, dynamical instability or ill-posedness result.
